original_question: For suitable phi, can one find an asymptotic formula with a small error term R_chi(h) for the count N(h; a_1, ..., a_d) of integer vectors (n_1, ..., n_d) with -h <= n_i <= h and fractional part {n_1 a_1 / N + ... + n_d a_d / N} < phi(n_1, ..., n_d), uniformly in the sense that for every chi < 1 the formula holds for at least chi N^d choices of (a_1, ..., a_d) with 0 <= a_i < N?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Open Problem 4 (page 7), introduced as a discrete diophantine-approximation statement that would be helpful for attacking Open Problems 1–3 and modeled on the Schmidt-type counting formula discussed earlier in Section 2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it uses the correct counting function N(h; a_1, ..., a_d), the correct box condition -h <= n_i <= h, the correct fractional-part inequality involving n_1 a_1/N + ... + n_d a_d/N, the right kind of main term built from phi, the paper's small error term R_chi(h), and the right average-type uniformity requirement that the formula hold for at least chi N^d choices of (a_1, ..., a_d) with 0 <= a_i < N. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
missing_details: The exact target is not a theorem or conjecture but Open Problem 4 in Section 2, and the nearby paragraph says it is intended as a discrete version of Schmidt's metrical counting result and as a tool for Open Problems 1–3; that motivation is part of the paper's intent. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The paper states the main term explicitly as sum_{-h <= n_1, ..., n_d < h} phi(n_1, ..., n_d); your draft says 'an asymptotic formula' but does not write the exact main term. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should quantify the ambient parameter N as a positive integer; the paper leaves this implicit in Open Problem 4 because N is already the modulus governing the choices 0 <= a_i < N. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The exact statement quantifies 'for all chi < 1 and all h in N'; your draft has the chi-quantifier but should also state the universal quantifier over h explicitly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
The paper writes the error term specifically as R_chi(h), so its dependence on h as well as chi should be retained exactly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
A faithful stand-alone rewrite should make the ambient set Z^d explicit and should note that {x} denotes fractional part. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The statement in the paper has a small asymmetry: the count is defined with -h <= n_i <= h, while the printed main-term sum is over -h <= n_1, ..., n_d < h. Since your goal is paper-faithfulness, this exact printed form should be preserved rather than silently normalized. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The paper deliberately leaves both 'suitable phi' and 'small' error term unspecified, so a faithful rewrite should not impose extra regularity or size assumptions on phi or R_chi(h) that the paper itself does not state. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
refined_question: For a fixed dimension d >= 1 and each positive integer N, can one find, for a suitable real-valued function phi on integer d-tuples, an asymptotic representation with a "small" error term R_chi(h) for N(h; a_1, ..., a_d) := # { (n_1, ..., n_d) in Z^d : -h <= n_i <= h for i = 1, ..., d and {n_1 a_1/N + n_2 a_2/N + ... + n_d a_d/N} < phi(n_1, ..., n_d) }, namely N(h; a_1, ..., a_d) = sum_{-h <= n_1, ..., n_d < h} phi(n_1, ..., n_d) + R_chi(h), in such a way that for every chi < 1 and every positive integer h this formula holds for at least chi N^d choices of (a_1, ..., a_d) with 0 <= a_i < N? Here {x} denotes fractional part. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
justification: The draft is targeting Open Problem 4 exactly, not a broader neighboring problem: Section 2 first recalls Schmidt's metrical formula N(h) = sum phi + R for almost all alpha, then explains that a discrete result of that type would be useful for Open Problem 1 (and analogously for Open Problems 2 and 3), and finally states Open Problem 4 with the same counting shape but with the discrete parameters (a_1, ..., a_d) modulo N. That is precisely the structure reproduced in your draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
